extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and litigators preparing or defending PTAB IPR/PGR proceedings (NYIPLA members, PTAB counsel, young lawyers)
extracted.subtask_description: A procedural checklist and timeline for preparing, filing, and litigating petitions and trials before the PTAB (IPR and PGR), including filing content rules, discovery, motions, oral argument, institution standards, rehearing, and final decision/Director review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition timing and eligibility (IPR/PGR/CBM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing when petitions may be filed: IPR may be filed from patent issue date; PGR may be filed within 9 months of issue date (post-AIA); CBMs are no longer available for new petitions (statutory period expired Sept. 16, 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite 37 C.F.R. § 42.102(a); note Pre-AIA exceptions (patents filed under 'first to invent' regime). For IPR: may be filed by the later of 9 months after issue date or termination of any PGR. Include applicable case citations noted (SweeGen decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Core items that must accompany a petition: Petition (and its content), Fees, Mandatory Notices, Designating Counsel, Parallel Petitions Ranking Statement, Supporting Declarations and Exhibits, Service Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this as a filing checklist; each listed item has specific sub-requirements (see separate criteria). Ensure all items are included at filing to avoid notices of defect or incomplete petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content: statement of precise relief and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each petition or motion must be filed as a separate paper and must include: (1) A statement of the precise relief requested; and (2) A full statement of the reasons for the relief requested, including a detailed explanation of the significance of the evidence including material facts, and the governing law, rules, and precedent." (37 C.F.R. § 42.22(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a succinct requested order plus a detailed, evidentiary statement of why relief should be granted. Provide statutory grounding and tie evidence to legal argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content: statutory grounds and claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition must specify the statutory grounds for the petition (e.g., IPR – 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 or 103; PGR – 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112, or 251) and must show how the PTAB should construe each claim (Phillips-type approach, not broadest reasonable construction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify the ground(s) and state the proposed claim construction under the Phillips framework. Explain how the construed claim is unpatentable under the cited statutory ground(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content: element-by-element mapping to prior art with exhibit citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition must explain where each claim element is found in the prior art—typically paragraph form (prior practice is claim charts)—and include specific citations to exhibit numbers for the supporting evidence. (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.104, 42.204)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide claim charts or clear paragraph-by-paragraph mappings; cite exhibits precisely (e.g., Ex1006). Avoid conclusory statements without exhibit references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional statement of material facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners may include a statement of material facts with the petition; this is not required. Statements should identify each fact in separate paragraphs, including specific citations to the supporting portions of the record. (37 C.F.R. § 42.22(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If included, format facts in numbered paragraphs and cite supporting record locations for each fact to aid institution analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard: IPR reasonable likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Director may not authorize an inter partes review to be instituted unless the Director determines that the information presented in the petition ... shows that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the petition." (35 U.S.C. § 314(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare evidence/arguments to meet the 'reasonable likelihood' threshold for at least one challenged claim; institution is discretionary and depends on the petition plus any preliminary response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard: PGR more-likely-than-not (and novel legal question)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Director may not authorize a post-grant review to be instituted unless the Director determines that the information presented in the petition ... would demonstrate that it is more likely than not that at least 1 of the claims challenged in the petition is unpatentable." (35 U.S.C. § 324(a)) — may also be satisfied if petition raises a novel or unsettled legal question important to other patents or applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PGR, show >50% likelihood of unpatentability or present an important novel legal issue; tailor the petition accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not notice pleading — include complete arguments and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB limits the petitioner to the challenge grounds identified in the petition. "To the extent possible, include detailed arguments and all evidence supporting any challenges." (PTAB Consolidated Trial Practice Guide November 2019)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put your best foot forward at filing; do not rely on later supplementation to meet institution thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition word count limits and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions are limited to: 14,000 words for IPRs and 18,700 words for PGRs. Word count limits do not include Table of Contents, Table of Authorities, Mandatory Notices, Certificates of service or word count, Appendix of exhibits or claim listings. Petitions must include a certification stating the number of words in the paper (37 C.F.R. § 42.24(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate word-count certification; PTAB will accept the stated word count unless there is evidence of abuse (excessive words in figures, deleting spacing, excessive acronyms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11-type signature certification
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers filed with the PTAB in a proceeding must comply with the signature requirements set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.18(a) (37 C.F.R. § 42.11(b)). By presenting a paper to the PTAB, an attorney, registered practitioner, or unrepresented party attests to compliance with the certification requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b) (37 C.F.R. § 42.11(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure counsel executes required certifications and that filings meet professional responsibility attestations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: amounts, payment timing, and refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies request fees and post-institution fees for IPR and PGR (e.g., IPR basic fee $19,000 + post-institution $22,500; additional claim fees apply). All fees must be paid up-front at time of filing. If trial is not instituted, petitioner may file a request for a refund of any post-institution fee paid. Fees are paid electronically on the USPTO website. (37 C.F.R. § 42.15)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute excess-claim charges; pay fees electronically and retain proof of payment. If trial not instituted, follow refund procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of payment acceptance (Fedwire confirmation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fedwire confirmation of payment constitutes sufficient evidence to demonstrate that the required fee accompanies a petition and that 'payment is received' under the regulations (Toshiba America v. Monument Peak Ventures, IPR2021-00330, Paper 20 (POP)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain and submit Fedwire confirmations when using real-time transfers as evidence of payment received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notices: content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition must include mandatory notices identifying each real party-in-interest, related judicial or administrative matters, lead and back-up counsel, and service information. Patent Owner must file the same mandatory notices within 21 days of service and must file revised notices within 21 days of any change. (37 C.F.R. § 42.8)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update mandatory notices promptly; if update occurs before institution and in good faith, petitioner may update without changing petition filing date (Adello Biologics precedent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designating counsel: lead and back-up counsel, power of attorney, pro hac vice
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must designate lead and at least one back-up counsel (37 C.F.R. § 42.10(a)). Power of attorney must be filed with designation unless counsel is already of record (37 C.F.R. § 42.10(b)). Board may recognize counsel pro hac vice; lead counsel must be a registered practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 42.10(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure lead counsel is registered and available; designate backups who can act; file power of attorney as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel petitions ranking statement
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one petition is filed, petitioners must submit a separate five-page filing ranking the petitions based on desired order of review. The filing must explain material differences between petitions (preferably in table form) and why the Board should institute two petitions if it determines one satisfies the institution threshold. (PTAB Consolidated Trial Practice Guide November 2019 at 59-61)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ranking statement to justify multiple petitions and clarify distinctories between them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting declarations and exhibits (typical exhibit list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical exhibits include: Ex1001 Patent in Suit; Ex1002 Expert Declaration; Ex1003 CV of Expert; Ex1004 Prosecution History; Ex1005 Parallel Litigation Documents; Ex1006 Prior Art Document; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number exhibits consistently, include necessary expert affidavits and supporting documents, and cite exhibits in petition text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements and certificate of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Service must be by means at least as fast and reliable as Priority Mail Express unless parties agree to electronic service. Each filed document must be served on each opposing party simultaneously with filing on counsel of record. Service must include a certificate of service stating the date and manner of service and the name and address of every person served. When filing exhibits separately, include a transmittal letter incorporating the certificate of service. (37 C.F.R. § 42.6(e))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow strict service timing and include complete certificate details; one transmittal letter may cover multiple exhibits but must list each exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-filing notices: Notice of Filing Date Accorded / Defective Petition / Incomplete Petition
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB will issue notices in the weeks following filing if it detects defects. Sample notices include: Notice of Filing Date Accorded; Notice of Defective Petition; Notice of Incomplete Petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to PTAB notices and correct non-substantive defects via motions to correct clerical errors where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to correct clerical mistakes (post-filing corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner may file a motion to correct a clerical or typographical mistake without changing the filing date of the petition. The motion must explain the nature of the error, timing between discovery and correction, prejudice to patent owner, and whether the corrections impact the proceeding. Corrections cannot add 'substantive new evidence.' (37 C.F.R. § 42.104(c); Sweegen precedent)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be candid about errors, document when discovered, and avoid attempts to add substantive arguments or evidence via corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial disclosures: Option 1 and Option 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Two options for mandatory initial disclosures: Option 1 (modeled after FRCP 26(a)(1)(A)) requires basic exchange (names, addresses, telephone numbers of individuals likely to have discoverable information; copies of documents a party may use). Option 2 includes Option 1 plus additional contacts for non-published prior art disclosures and additional information regarding secondary considerations of non-obviousness if relevant. If parties agree, submit the agreement by the earlier of the patent owner’s preliminary response filing or the preliminary response due date (37 C.F.R. § 42.51(a)(1)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiate initial-disclosure scope early; if no agreement, expect motions to obtain discovery (37 C.F.R. § 42.51(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Preliminary Response (POPR): scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may file a POPR within three months of PTAB’s notice according a filing date. POPR is limited to stating reasons why PTAB should not institute trial; may present supporting evidence including new testimonial testimony; may not include any amendment; may disclaim challenged claims (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.107, 42.207).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners can present evidence to defeat institution but cannot amend. If disclaimed, claim preclusion applies (precedential authority cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies and sur-replies to POPR: leave, timing, and word limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners may seek leave to file a reply to the POPR; Board may grant upon showing good cause. Replies limited to arguments raised in POPR and to 5,600 words. Replies due one month after service of POPR (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.23, 42.24, 42.108). Patent owner may seek to file a sur-reply to the POPR limited to 5,600 words (37 C.F.R. § 42.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek leave timely and confine replies to issues raised; monitor shortened schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution timing: PTAB decision deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB must determine whether to institute a trial within three months of the earlier of the patent owner’s preliminary response filing or the preliminary response due date. (Trial Practice Guide, 77 Fed. Reg. at 48757)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for institution decision on a compressed timeline and file necessary papers to meet that schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAS/all-claims rule on institution
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner 'is entitled to a final written decision addressing all of the claims it has challenged.' SAS Institute Inc. v. Iancu, 138 S. Ct. 1348 (2018). The Board will also proceed on all grounds of unpatentability for each challenged claim when instituting a trial (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.108(a), 208(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When challenging multiple claims, expect institution (if granted) to cover all challenged claims and grounds raised in the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary denials: General Plastic factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors the PTAB considers in exercising discretion (from General Plastic): prior petitions by same petitioner against same claims; whether petitioner knew or should have known of asserted prior art when filing first petition; whether petitioner had patent owner’s preliminary response or PTAB decision on first petition; time between learning of prior art and filing second petition; explanation for delay between multiple petitions; PTAB resources and the one-year statutory deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these factors proactively when filing follow-on petitions to avoid discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary analysis when prior art overlaps: Becton Dickinson factors
rubrics_metrics.description: When presented with prior art similar to previously cited art, the PTAB considers similarities and material differences; cumulative nature; extent previously evaluated; overlap between arguments and how petitioner relies on/distinguishes prior art; whether petitioner explained how USPTO erred; whether additional evidence justifies reconsideration. (Becton, Dickinson v. B. Braun Melsungen AG)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain novel factual differences and why reconsideration is warranted; identify additional evidence distinguishing the new art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factors for parallel district court litigation (and USPTO clarifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: For proceedings parallel with district court litigation, PTAB considers: whether the court granted a stay or one may be granted; proximity of the court’s trial date to PTAB's projected deadline; speed of district court resolution; investment in parallel proceeding; overlap between issues; whether parties are the same; other circumstances including merits. USPTO clarified exceptions where Fintiv denial is inappropriate (e.g., petition presents compelling evidence of unpatentability; denial based on ITC proceeding; petitioner stipulates not to pursue parallel district court grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parallel litigation exists, analyze Fintiv factors and consider stipulations or strong unpatentability evidence to mitigate Fintiv denial risk. See Apple v. Fintiv and USPTO interim guidance (Press Release 22-14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing requests after institution or denial: timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: For decisions not to institute trial, petitioner may file a rehearing request within 30 days of PTAB entry of its decision; for decisions to institute, rehearing must be filed within 14 days. The rehearing request must specifically identify all matters the PTAB misapprehended or overlooked and where each matter was previously addressed in a motion, opposition, or reply (37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly map each alleged error to the prior record; follow strict timing. Oppositions and replies to rehearing follow one-month and one-month cycles (with authorization requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery by Patent Owner and Petitioner (scheduling and motions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduling order specifies discovery timelines. Discovery includes agreed initial disclosures and mandatory notices, routine discovery, and additional discovery that requires party agreement or a patent owner motion. Parties may file motions to obtain discovery (37 C.F.R. § 42.51).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan discovery carefully per scheduling order; if additional discovery is needed, move promptly explaining necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions (cross-examination) and uncompelled testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may depose declarants who submit affidavit testimony. A party seeking a deposition must file a notice at least ten business days before the deposition. Cross-examination should occur after supplemental evidence is due and conclude more than one week before filing papers that cite the testimony. Testimony must be filed as an exhibit, but either party may file the testimony. (37 C.F.R. § 42.53)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule depositions to permit use in later briefs; observe filing-as-exhibit rules and cross-exam timing restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to evidence: timing and supplementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to deposition evidence must be made during the deposition. Objections to other evidence must be filed within five business days of service of the evidence, except that objections to evidence submitted before institution should be made within ten business days of institution. Parties may file supplemental evidence in response to objections within ten business days of service of the objection. (37 C.F.R. § 42.64)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track evidence service dates closely to meet objection windows; use supplemental-evidence windows to address disputed items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Response post-institution: timing, content, and exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Owner may file, within 3 months of institution, a response to substantively challenge the claims. Responses are limited to 14,000 words for IPRs and 18,700 words for PGRs. The response may contain exhibits or claim listings attached as appendices (35 U.S.C. §§ 316(a)(8), 326(a)(8); 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.120, 42.220; 37 C.F.R. § 42.24(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a full substantive defense within word limits and include expert declarations/exhibits (e.g., Ex2001, Ex2002).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend claims: limits and support requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may file a motion to amend instituted claims (typically due three months after institution). A motion to amend may not enlarge claim scope or add new matter and must clearly identify support for the amended claims in the original patent disclosure (35 U.S.C. §§ 316(d)(3), 326(d)(3); 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.121(a), 42.221(a)). Motions to amend are limited to 25 pages (37 C.F.R. § 42.24(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit citations to original disclosure for each amended limitation; adhere to page limits. Consider pilot program options and related studies (USPTO MTA Study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner replies and timing in the main trial period
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical timeline: petitioner reply to patent owner response and opposition to motion to amend are due 3 months after the patent owner filing; petitioner reply to opposition and to motion to amend and other replies follow schedule set in the scheduling order (see timeline boxes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor scheduling order dates; prepare reply briefs within the specified timeframes and word limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sur-replies: authorization and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Sur-replies responding to motions are not generally permitted but may be authorized; sur-replies may not be accompanied by new evidence other than deposition transcripts of reply witness cross-examination. Sur-replies to motions to amend are limited to 12 pages unless PTAB orders otherwise (37 C.F.R. § 42.23; Consolidated Trial Practice Guide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request authorization if necessary and keep sur-replies concise and confined to the proper scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to exclude evidence: content and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to exclude must identify where in the record the objection originally was made, identify where in the record the evidence sought to be excluded was relied on by an opponent, address objections to exhibits in numerical order, and explain each objection. Scheduling order typically sets deadline (usually about one month after P.O. reply in support of motion to amend) with short opposition/reply windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize objections clearly by exhibit number and cite original record locations; anticipate quick turnaround on oppositions and replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument: request, demonstratives, and pre-hearing conference
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request oral argument on an issue raised in a paper; the request must be a separate paper specifying the issues. Demonstrative exhibits must be served at least seven business days before the oral argument and filed no later than the time of the oral argument. Parties may request a pre-hearing conference call (generally no later than three business days prior to hearing). (37 C.F.R. § 42.70)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File oral-argument requests separately and serve demonstratives on time; consider a pre-hearing call to clarify issues and panel expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP program for less-experienced advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAP (Legal Experience and Advancement Program) grants additional oral-argument time (typically 15 minutes) to qualifying patent agents/attorneys with three or fewer substantive oral arguments in any federal tribunal and seven or fewer years of experience as a licensed attorney or registered patent agent. Application must be made after hearing date is set, via PTABHearings@uspto.gov at least five business days before the hearing with a Request and Verification Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible practitioners should apply early to get extra time; more experienced counsel may assist limitedly on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision: timing and permissible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB must enter a final written decision no later than one year after instituting trial; Director may extend by not more than 6 months for good cause (35 U.S.C. §§ 316(a)(11), 326(a)(11)). In an IPR, PTAB may cancel claims as anticipated (§102) or obvious (§103). In PGR, PTAB may cancel claims for §102/103, §101, §112, or §251 grounds. PTAB may cancel all or some reviewed claims or incorporate new/amended claims determined to be patentable (35 U.S.C. §§ 318(a)-(b), 328(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for a final decision within statutory deadline; motions to amend and evidentiary records should support desired final outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Director review process: who, timing, and content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim Director review allows the Director to sua sponte initiate review of a PTAB final written decision. A party may request Director review within 30 days of the final written decision or decision granting rehearing. Requests are publicly posted; denials and grants follow multi-week timelines. Requests may not introduce new evidence or arguments and are limited to 15 pages; email to Director_PTABDecision_Review@uspto.gov must include a priority-ranked list of issues and brief explanations. Grounds that may warrant review include intervening change in law, novel legal issues, material errors of fact or law, matters misapprehended or overlooked, issues of importance to the Office or patent community, and inconsistencies with Office procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Director review sparingly; prioritize issues and explain importance concisely within page limits. Track public status pages for requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word and page limits for assorted filings (replies, sur-replies, motions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific limits noted: replies to POPR limited to 5,600 words; sur-replies to POPR limited to 5,600 words; replies are due one month after service; motion to amend limited to 25 pages; sur-replies to motions to amend limited to 12 pages; normal petition/POPR word limits (14,000 IPR / 18,700 PGR) apply elsewhere (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.23-25, 42.24(a),(b),(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track which limits apply to each filing; exclude enumerated items (TOC, TOA, mandatory notices, certificates, appendix exhibits) from word counts as specified.
